answers.answer: An Exile who takes Oathkeeper during Act cannot win at the next Wake: the Usurper check occurs before the title flips. At that next Wake they flip the title to Usurper; they can first win at the following Wake, or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while they still hold it. Losing the title prevents the Usurper win; retaking it resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Title transfer and victory timing: “Victory was checked before this flip”; “win at the following Wake or at the end of round 8”.

answers.answer: Oath of Supremacy matches Vision of Conquest (rule the most sites); Oath of the People matches Vision of Rebellion (hold People's Favor); Oath of Protection matches Vision of Sanctuary (hold the most relics and banners combined); Oath of Devotion matches Vision of Faith (hold Darkest Secret). For a Visionary win, an Exile must have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions must have been drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest/Sanctuary, “most” means strictly more than every other player; ties do not count.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths; Visionary victory: “strictly more than every other player, no ties” and at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: end die at ends of rounds 5/6/7 only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper; thresholds 6 / 5–6 / 3–6.

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins—Chancellor unless a qualified Citizen meets the Successor goal, in which case that Citizen wins alone; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions resolved Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, Chancellor unless a qualified Citizen meets Successor. This fallback applies even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper. Holding the Successor goal alone does not end the game.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion, priority 1–4.

answers.answer: The Citizen Successor goals are: Supremacy—hold more relics and banners combined than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; People—hold Darkest Secret; Protection—hold People's Favor; Devotion—hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a true Vision or by becoming Usurper.
answers.evidence: Citizen succession table; “Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.”

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: if it has 1, you must add if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After the choice(s), if it has 6+ favor, flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this last step does not cause another payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake, step 1: exact payment/return choices, last-favor restriction, Mob repeats once, threshold checked afterward.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Exile/Chancellor based on warbands remaining in personal bank, while Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost; (4) save unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); (5) optional Rest powers, each once in chosen order. Supply refresh values: Chancellor 18+ = 6, 11–17 = 5, 4–10 = 4, 0–3 = 3; Exile 9+ = 6, 4–8 = 5, 0–3 = 4.
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order steps 1–5; “Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space”; save remaining Supply one extra space per unspent Supply.

answers.answer: Search costs 2–4 Supply and uses either the world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck Search costs 2 with zero Visions drawn, 3 with 1–2, and 4 with 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3 (fewer only if source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw); do not voluntarily stop early. A Vision drawn from the world deck is announced as a Vision (not necessarily named), immediately stops the draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. Drawing a Vision from a discard pile neither stops drawing nor advances the track.
answers.evidence: Search section: sources, costs, draw procedure, and distinction between world-deck and discard Visions.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, ordering multiple discards as you choose. For cards from hand/advisers, use the pile based on your pawn's region: Cradle pawn → Provinces pile; Provinces → Hinterland; Hinterland → Cradle; never the same-region pile. When discarding a card at a site in another region, apply the cycle to that card's region, not your pawn's. Favor on discarded cards immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations: cycle and remote-site rule; card resources return/transfer immediately as specified.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup and facedown together. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser as permitted, respecting locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, check against the new limit before playing it and use the lowest of multiple limits. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card, including site-only cards and Visions, may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action; faceup advisers cannot be discarded at will, only when a rule permits or requires it. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup into the separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding their old revealed Vision; it does not use an adviser slot. Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search—Adviser and True Vision; Adviser state table.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply. Put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (no favor or secrets already) and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; Citizens gain purple. Relics and ruins are ineligible; site rule is not required, but a remote ruled site does not permit Muster. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site (no relics/ruins). Either put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from its suit bank, or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 secret from the shared bank per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers never match; with no matching advisers, the second option gains zero secrets, but its 2-favor cost remains payable. Finite favor/warband supplies limit gains to what is available; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Relics held by players or in the Reliquary cannot be recovered. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds, put your payment on it, distribute its old favor singly among suit banks starting at any chosen bank and proceeding away from the world deck in printed order with wraparound, and flip it to normal if Mob; no seizure penalty applies. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds, put the payment on it, the new holder takes 1 old secret, and the previous holder takes the rest; if recovering from yourself, all old secrets return to you, and from the shared bank the remainder stays there.
answers.evidence: Recover—cost and banner rules.

answers.answer: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, their pawn's site must contain at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such mismatching card is enough even if other cards match. If the holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, that card matches none and the banner is recoverable. An empty site or ruin-only site protects the banner because there is no suited card. Recovering it from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata.

answers.answer: Choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map (one defense die each). If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the required local target.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2: defender and target selection.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Defense is shields rolled (each double-symbol doubles shields, stacking), plus all defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Each attack skull immediately kills 1 of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, with a lone hollow sword adding zero. An attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never excess. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower loses.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4–5.

answers.answer: After attacker victory, first the defender kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. Zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. For any seized banner (by any means except Recover), burn 2 of its resources down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker's destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses the destination. Then resolve the attacker's victorious battle-plan effects; finally discard plans saying “At end, discard.”
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8: defeat before targets, target resolution, victory effects and end discards.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. The defending side shares relevant powers/modifiers; Chancellor's Oathkeeper defense bonus is shared even outside Supremacy. Allied board warbands add defense only if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; each shared plan can be used only once per Campaign by one user, who pays. The declared defender chooses order/timing/priority if Allies disagree, and Chancellor chooses which Imperial defenders' warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizens' board warbands stay there. A Citizen attacking the Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.
answers.evidence: Campaign—Imperial defense and steps 1, 6.

answers.answer: Base Supply costs by origin and destination region are: from Cradle to Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces to Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; from Hinterland to Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. Reveal a facedown destination and place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck. Apply the fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override: a power saying spend no Supply makes the cost zero even if another power increases it, including banishment. Site-entry restrictions remain unless ignored by the named rule/power.
answers.evidence: Travel section and cost table; Travel cost order.

answers.answer: In play, the Grand Scepter holder cannot make an offer on the turn they took it. On a later turn, the holder—even an Exile—may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the Exile flips to Citizen, replaces all their board/map warbands with purple (if short, they choose which to remove and replace), discards their revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if it is their turn, and refreshes to full leftmost Supply. They exchange the promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Only actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play—Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance.

answers.answer: In the Chronicle, a victory by Vision alone sets the next Oath to match that Vision. Any other victory method, or multiple victory methods, allows the winner to choose any Oath except the current one. Chronicle Citizenship is a separate free offer: if the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed, to Exile, then the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles (not themself); each accepting Exile flips their board to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. To rebuild the world deck, shuffle all denizens remaining in play (excluding cards retained at sites, in Archive, or Dispossessed); stack 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions on top (12 cards), then 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), then remaining denizens below. The Chronicle aid's “12 denizens + 2” is incorrect; the correct top stack is 10 + 2 = 12.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle steps 1–2 and 9.
